body:
`scripts/cover_enforcer.py` acquires an exclusive lock at MODULE SCOPE (line
103), not inside `main()`:

    lock = open(tempfile.gettempdir() + '/cover_enforcer.lock', 'x')
    ...
    except FileExistsError:
        sys.exit(2)

and releases it via `atexit.register(removeLock)` (line 114).

`atexit` does not run on SIGKILL or a hard crash. The autopilot tick runs its
LLM phase under a `timeout` and has been killed mid-run repeatedly (12 times in
the 8 days to 2026-08-03, per notes), so the lock leaks in practice — not in
theory. Observed today: a zero-byte `/var/folders/.../T/cover_enforcer.lock`
dated 2026-08-07 00:28, left by an earlier run.

Because the lock is taken at import, any test that imports the module then dies
at import with `SystemExit: 2`. That reddens
`tests/unit/test_802_metadata_change_dispatch.py::
test_enforcer_missing_log_logs_single_info_not_warning_spam` on a tree whose
code is fine. Verified both directions: the test fails identically on
`origin/main` in a clean worktree, and passes immediately after `rm` of the
stale lock. Nothing about the repository contents changed.

CI never sees it — each run gets a fresh container with an empty tempdir — so
this is invisible to the merge gate and lands entirely on local runs.

Why it matters beyond one red test: `scripts/test-autopilot.sh` preflight gates
the tick on a green suite, so a tick killed by its own timeout can leave behind
an artifact that fails the preflight of every subsequent tick. That is the
self-locking-wedge shape — a failure whose repair is blocked by the failure —
and the fact that it is one `rm` away is exactly what makes it expensive to
diagnose rather than expensive to fix.

Two candidate repairs, neither applied here:
1. Move the lock acquisition out of module scope into the CLI entry point, so
   importing the module for a test never takes it. This is the real fix — a
   test has no business contending for a runtime singleton.
2. Make the lock stale-aware: write the pid, and on FileExistsError treat a
   lock whose pid is not alive as abandoned rather than as a running instance.
   Worth doing regardless, because the same leak blocks the actual
   cover-enforcer service after any unclean shutdown, not just tests.

Separately and unrelated to the lock: the same suite's
`tests/unit/test_ingest_batch_dirty.py::
test_successful_import_marks_batch_dirty_without_hot_loop_http_calls` fails
locally with `sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file` from
`scripts/cwa_db.py:107`, because the db path it composes only exists inside the
container. Also pre-existing on `origin/main`, also invisible in CI. Filed here
so the pair is not rediscovered as "main is red".
title: cover_enforcer.py takes an import-time lock released only by atexit, so a killed process reddens every later test run
